title: Cleaning passenger and goods lift interiors
audience: Cleaning operative cleaning the interior of a lift car in a building, under the building's approved procedure and with the building manager's permission.
learningOutcomes: Obtain permission and isolate a lift for cleaning with the doors open, so the worker is not in a confined space.
Select the cleaning material for each lift surface: car walls, handrails, doors, floor, tracks and control panel.
Clean the doors and door tracks inside and out, and vacuum the floor tracks, without pressing any call button.
Return the lift to service and record the job, scheduling the work to cause minimal inconvenience to the building.

instruction.heading: Scope and the boundary of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers cleaning the interior surfaces of a lift car, the landing door faces and tracks that can be reached safely, and the control panel surfaces. It does not cover opening the lift shaft, working in the lift pit or machine room, or adjusting or repairing any lift component. Those tasks are mechanical or electrical work that belongs to the lift service provider. Completing this lesson does not grant a licence or authority for that work.

instruction.heading: Permission and timing
instruction.body: Always ask the building's responsible person for permission before isolating a lift. Where a passenger lift is used by staff and visitors, schedule the internal clean at a time that causes the least disruption to the people working in the building. The isolation step should be done only after the permission is confirmed and recorded.

instruction.heading: Isolating the lift safely
instruction.body: Isolate the lift with the doors open, so that you are not working in a confined space and so that the lift is safe to enter. Use the lift's isolating switch to take the car out of service, following the building's procedure. Keep the control buttons in mind during isolation: the call button must not be pressed while you are working, because it would bring the lift back into use or send it to a floor while you are inside. Confirm the lift is isolated before you enter the car.

instruction.heading: Equipment and electrical checks
instruction.body: Before using the vacuum cleaner, check that it has a current electrical safety test date recorded on the site register. Inspect the plug and lead for damage, bare wires or tape repairs. Check the bag and filter, since a blocked filter can make the vacuum overheat. Check the hose for blockages and set the beater bar height for the floor covering. Confirm that every chemical has a legible label. Only trained employees may use electrical equipment. Repeat the safety checks at the end of the task. Wash and dry cloths and tools, and keep them colour coded.

instruction.heading: Choosing materials for each surface
instruction.body: Identify the dirt on each surface first. Dirt on the car walls, handrails, doors and control panel may need a different product from the dirt on the floor. Choose the material that suits each surface from the approved product list, and use the same wall-washing method used for other walls in the building. Use the same floor methods used for other hard and carpeted floors, selected by the floor covering in the car. The source names mop sweeping, single-solution mopping and suction cleaning as the methods for these floors; the full methods are not written in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Cleaning the car and doors
instruction.body: Clean the car walls, then clean the handrails and control panel with care, wiping the buttons with a lightly dampened cloth so that no liquid enters the panel. Clean the car floor using the method for its covering. Clean the doors inside and outside to remove marks and fingerprints. Clean around the door tracks and frames, and vacuum the floor tracks to remove dirt and dust. Be careful not to press any call button on the control panel while you work.

instruction.heading: Returning the lift to service
instruction.body: When the clean is finished, check that all cloths, tools and vacuum cleaners have been removed from the car and the landing area. Return the lift to service by changing the isolating switch back, following the building's procedure. The source wording on this step is unclear about the switch position, so the building's written procedure must be checked before this lesson is used. Confirm that the lift responds normally, and record the job.

instruction.heading: Storing equipment and finishing
instruction.body: Safety check and damp wipe the vacuum cleaner after use. Empty the rubbish according to the building's waste disposal procedure. Clean the dust pan and brush and store them by colour. Clean materials and well-maintained machines last longer and keep the service consistent.

procedure: Confirm the lift cleaning permission and timing with the building's responsible person, and record it.
Check the vacuum cleaner's electrical safety test status and inspect the plug, lead, bag, filter and hose.
Confirm the approved materials for each lift surface and check every chemical label.
Put on gloves and eye protection, and open ventilation where the building allows it.
Isolate the lift with the doors open, following the building's isolating procedure, and confirm it is isolated before entering the car.
Identify the dirt on the car walls, handrails, doors and control panel, and select the material for each surface.
Clean the car walls, handrails and control panel, keeping liquid out of the panel.
Clean the car floor using the method for its covering.
Clean the doors inside and outside, then clean the door tracks and frames and vacuum the floor tracks.
Do not press any call button while working inside the car.
Remove all equipment from the car and landing, then return the lift to service following the building's procedure.
Safety check and damp wipe the vacuum, empty the rubbish, store the equipment by colour, and record the job.

workedExamples.situation: A worker has been asked to clean a lift car in a five-storey office building during the working day. The lift is busy, and the building manager is available by phone.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the worker do before isolating the lift, and when?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker confirms the permission with the building manager and agrees a time that causes the least disruption, such as a quieter period. The worker then isolates the lift with the doors open, following the building procedure, and confirms it is isolated before going into the car. Cleaning during the busiest period would put people in the building at risk of an unexpected lift movement and would cause avoidable disruption.

workedExamples.situation: While wiping the control panel, the worker's cloth catches the call button and a light comes on.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the worker do next, and how do they keep the panel clean?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker stops, does not press any further buttons, and checks the lift state with the building procedure. The worker should use a lightly dampened cloth, wipe around the buttons rather than pressing them, and keep liquid out of the panel. The event is recorded and reported to the building manager.

equipmentAndPpe: Vacuum cleaner with a current electrical safety test status and a checked bag, filter and hose
Approved cleaning materials for walls, metal, doors, floors and tracks, each labelled
Gloves and eye protection suitable for the products used
Warning signs for the lift entrance

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the car without permission or without isolating it.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm permission with the building's responsible person and follow the isolation procedure before you enter.

commonErrors.error: Pressing a call button, or letting liquid into the control panel.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not press any button while working inside the car, and use a lightly dampened cloth around the buttons.

commonErrors.error: Leaving equipment in the car or landing when the lift is returned to service.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the car and landing for all cloths, tools and vacuum cleaners before returning the lift to service.

commonErrors.error: Working on lift mechanisms, shaft or cables while cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Stay within the car interior and the reachable door faces and tracks. Report any mechanical fault rather than attempting repair.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Only trained employees may use electrical equipment. This lesson does not certify you to use the vacuum or to work on lift equipment.
Lift servicing, repair and work inside the shaft or machine room are outside this lesson. This lesson does not grant it.
Electrical equipment must be tested and tagged, or inspected, under the local rule.
Chemicals must be used as their label directs, with the safety data sheet available on site.
Stop and report if the lift does not isolate or return to service properly, if a call button activates during work, or if a fault is found.

qualityStandard: Permission was confirmed and the isolation was done with the doors open before entering the car.
Car walls, handrails, doors, floor, control panel and door tracks are clean with no fingerprints or marks left.
No liquid entered the control panel and no call button was pressed during the work.
No equipment or waste is left in the car or on the landing when the lift returns to service.
The lift responds normally after return to service, and the job is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Record of permission and timing from the building's responsible person
Vacuum pre-use and end-of-use check record
Chemical product and label reference for each surface
Record of isolation and return to service, with the time
Any fault, damage or unexpected lift movement reported to the building manager
summary: Get permission and isolate the lift with the doors open before you enter the car.
Match the material to each surface, and never press a call button while working inside.
Check the car, landing and tracks for equipment and waste, then return the lift to service through the building's procedure.
Lift servicing and mechanical work are outside this lesson and need the appropriate licence or authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before cleaning inside a lift car, what must happen first?
options: Press the call button to check that the lift is working before you go in
Obtain the building's permission and isolate the lift with the doors open
Close the doors and clean from the outside only and work from the lobby floor
Remove the control panel so it can be cleaned separately while the car stays in use

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must care be taken with the control buttons during a lift clean?
options: They cannot be cleaned with any product because they are electrical and are never wiped down
They must stay hygienic because many people touch them, and no call button may be pressed while cleaning
They are sealed, so they are cleaned only once a year and only by the building's own contractor
They are the personal property of the building manager and must not be touched by any cleaner

knowledgeChecks.question: Which task falls outside the scope of this lift cleaning lesson?
options: Cleaning the car walls and handrails
Vacuuming the floor tracks and cleaning the door faces
Opening the lift shaft or working on lift mechanisms
Checking that the vacuum cleaner's plug and lead are safe
